meta.title: Directions for the Old Town Walk

paragraphs: How to Walk the Old Town Path, posted by Lily. On Thursday, Teacher Kim said, "Please write directions for the new Explorers." The Explorers like to walk in the old town on Saturday morning. Mia and Leo walked the path with me. Leo drew a small map. Now you can follow my directions, too. Do you have a pencil?

Start at the bus stop in front of the town library. Walk to the corner, and turn left into the old street. You will pass a small post office on your right. After a few steps, you will arrive at a zebra crossing. Cross the road. Then walk on the path next to the wall. The path is small, so walk slowly and stay on the left.

The old bridge is at the end of the path. The old bridge has walls of gray stone. It is very short. A small stream runs under the bridge. You can see little fish in it. Cross the bridge. At the other side, turn right. The mug shop is the second shop on the left. It has a blue door. The woman in the shop makes the mugs by hand. Mia bought a mug with a small green frog on it.

Next, walk to the end of the street. A small store stands on the corner. It sells cold water and fruit. Leo bought a bottle of water. I bought a small bag of mango. Sit next to the store for a few minutes. Then you are ready to return. To return to the bus stop, go the same way back.

Walk back over the bridge. Walk along the path, and cross the road at the zebra crossing. You will pass the post office again, but now it is on your left. Then you will arrive at the corner. Turn right, and the bus stop is in front of the library. The walk took us about forty minutes with all the stops. Teacher Kim read my post. She smiled. "Your directions are clear," she said, "and the little map helps a lot."
text.summary: Lily writes a blog post with directions for a walk in the old town. The walk goes from the bus stop to a bridge, a mug shop, and a small store, and then it returns to the bus stop.
